access.notes: Produced by the CommandAGI stack; pulled from its own R2 buckets with an account token. Not public.

commandagi-kg.description: The production long-term-memory graph: 3.05M nodes and 5.20M edges across four cliques, with the full event log behind them. Held here in three storage formats -- the cold-tier NDJSON/parquet export, the same tables as Iceberg, and the hot-tier D1 SQL dump.
commandagi-kg.notes: **Three storage formats of one graph, not three sources.** Counts agreeing across graph/, __r2_data_catalog/ and d1/ are ONE fact confirmed by construction, and quoting them as three independent verifications is exactly the composite-source double-count this federation layer refuses. Redistribution is prohibited, so every artifact derived from it inherits prohibited through the licence closure -- which is computed, not authored.

__r2_data_catalog.description: The same graph as Iceberg tables. NOT an independent observation of it.

_acquisition.description: The staging README, file inventory and download script that produced this pull.

d1.description: Hot-tier D1 SQL dump. A bounded cache over the cold tier, demoted from source-of-truth. Also NOT independent.

graph/clique.description: Per-clique projection snapshots: the authoritative current node and edge state, plus DuckDB-compacted parquet adjacency.

graph/log.description: The full event log by sequence -- history, provenance and causal chain. This is the derivation record, not a second copy of the state.

commandagi-kg.title: CommandAGI knowledge graph (cold tier)

access.notes: Produced by the CommandAGI stack; pulled from its own R2 buckets with an account token. Not public.

commandagi-kg-dev.description: The development stack's cold bucket. A near-empty graph beside a real one.
commandagi-kg-dev.notes: Registered as its own source rather than folded into commandagi-kg so that a count taken over 'the CommandAGI graph' cannot silently include a dev stack. A control that shares a name with its treatment is how the two come to drift together.
commandagi-kg-dev.title: CommandAGI knowledge graph (dev stack, cold tier)

courtlistener.description: US court opinions and the citation network between them.

license.name: US court opinions are public domain; CourtListener's own metadata is separately licensed and has not been established

courtlistener.notes: **Attribution is a hypothesis.** The staged parquet uses the id namespace `kg:clop:`, which is consistent with CourtListener opinion ids, and the table shape (a `cites-precedent` citation map) matches. The pull recorded no upstream release, so this card asserts the hypothesis and marks it as one rather than quietly becoming the provenance of everything derived from it.
courtlistener.title: CourtListener (hypothesis)

cskg.description: The consolidated commonsense graph over ConceptNet 5.7, WordNet 3.0, ATOMIC, FrameNet, Roget, Visual Genome and Wikidata-CS. Already vendored here in a narrow projection; this is the fuller staged cut.
cskg.notes: **The vendored copy in symbolic_ai_kg/data/ is a selectional projection, not this.** It collapses concepts by lemma, reads only selected relations and maps them into a small local relation set. Calling that projection 'CSKG' is the same class of error as calling a slice a result, and it is renamed cskg_selectional_v1 for exactly that reason. CSKG is itself a composite of seven upstreams, so an assertion ingested both directly and through CSKG is ONE observation seen twice -- see the double-counting test.
cskg.title: CSKG (Commonsense Knowledge Graph)

fec.description: Campaign contribution records and the committees and donors behind them.
fec.title: US Federal Election Commission

gdelt.description: Global event records and actor tables extracted from world news, with country and name resolution. The staged cut is several overlapping windows.

license.name: GDELT Project terms of use (free use with attribution)

gdelt.notes: The windows OVERLAP (7/14/30/60 day cuts taken on different dates). Pooling them without deduplicating by event id double-counts the intersection, and the intersection is the majority of the smaller windows. This is recorded here rather than in a downstream script because the next reader will not know.
gdelt.title: GDELT Project

license.name: Project Gutenberg terms; catalogue feeds offered for free use

gutenberg.notes: Redistribution is recorded as unresolved rather than permitted. openalex.description: An open index of scholarly works, authors, institutions, sources, topics and funders, and the citation graph over them. Used here as a large, genuinely open relation network with real entity identity -- the property the vendored WordNet projection does not have.

openflights.description: Airports, airlines and the route network between them. Small, and the cleanest available example of a genuinely cyclic relation_network -- which is the topology the world IR exists to represent and the flow DAG refuses.
